```
C:\builds\wireshark\wireshark\epan\epan.c(82,10): fatal error C1083: Cannot open include file: 'zstd.h': No such file or directory [C:\builds\wireshark\wireshark\build\epan\epan.vcxproj]

```
The LZ4 and Zstd versions should be added to `epan_get_runtime_version_info` instead.

> The LZ4 and Zstd versions should be added to `epan_get_runtime_version_info` instead.

+1 - if a header file provides a version number, that should be shown in "Compiled with ...", as that's what was used at compile time and may not match what's being used at run time, and if an API routine provides a version number, that should be shown in "Running with..." as, if it's from a dynamically-linked/shared library, what's used at run time may not match what was used at compile time.
mentioned in commit boolean263/wireshark@5de4d2ebbb4e5c4762e134c50456ce187bb056ea

added 1 commit
  • 5de4d2eb - Move LZ4 and Zstd from compile-time to runtime info
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3026/diffs?diff_id=187919367&start_sha=abd6f3aca6d5a91af1eee6a4a278704ac4559f5d)

Wait, don't remove the whole "compiled with" information either, just leave it as is.

The current logic is (taking for example LZ4) "the program was compiled with the LZ4 decompression feature enabled" (compile time version for the dependency may be displayed if it exists, this version is not very useful and should be omitted in most cases IMO) and "the program is running with the LZ4 library dependency version XX" (version very useful).

The whole feature vs dependency (compile-time vs run-time) distinction alluded above is somewhat muddled by the same format but that is the gist. There are some redundancies and inconsistencies because loading the dependency also implies that the optional feature is enabled (where it exists), but that is a separate issue and should be left for a separate MR.

Hope that was clear. Just leave the LZ4 and Zstd compile time information as is for now please. Propose format and style changes in a separate MR if you wish.

How's this then? I've left the LZ4 and Zstd compile time information in place; I also found that both have macros for their compile-time versions, so I added those. I still added LZ4 and Zstd to the run-time information as well with their run-time versions, so differences can be seen if any.

I didn't raise this issue but I should've. Given that the compile version is not useful, and `PACKAGE_VERSION` is an odd name that should not even be public because of collisions, and libmaxminddb is incompatible with GPL 2.0 and only used with mmdbresolve, and that it only works on Windows, we should probably remove that.
